items.title: Growing with Care: Plan and Budget 2024
notes:
Craig Dyer, Commissioner, Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer commenced the presentation, by delivering an overview of the Budget Committee review process, the strategic plan for 2023-2027 and the preliminary 2024 operating budget.

Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner, Public Health & Paramedic Services/Medical Officer of Health continued the presentation, addressing equitable services and opportunities. Fauzia Baig, Director, Equity, Diversity & Inclusion, elaborated by speaking on the COVID-19 rollout within the Region and current 2024 service levels. Paula Whitlow, Director, Truth and Reconciliation furthered the presentation by discussing the strategic initiatives related to equitable services and opportunities. 

Peter Sweeney, Commissioner, Community Services, addressed equitable services and opportunities within children's services highlighting the Canada-Wide Early Learning and Child Care (CWELLC) program and proposed budget changes. Cheryl Braan, Director, Corporate Services, provided additional insights into the children's services budget.

Dr. Wang addressed the two phases of proposed 2024 service enhancements for Paramedic Services. She highlighted that these enhancements were rescheduled to January 1st to mitigate the impact on the 2024 budget. Additionally, she discussed vehicle response rates by year, unit utilization (ambulance use) by month, and the frequency and duration of code yellow and code red status events. Dr. Wang noted that both code yellow and code red events were less frequent but longer in duration during the first three quarters of 2023 compared to the same period in 2022. Continuing the presentation, C. Braan provided further insights into the 2024 Paramedic Services budget. She emphasized that Paramedic Services has a 10-year capital program amounting to approximately $106 million.

In response to a question from the Committee, Police Chief Mark Crowell provided clarification on the median duration of code yellow and code red status events. He further specified that, over the course of the year, there has been a reduction in offload delays, underscoring that this is not the predominant factor contributing to code reds/yellows.

Chief Crowell addressed a committee question regarding factors influencing response times and the current dispatch system. He emphasized that response time does not solely determine the success of paramedic services. Furthermore, he discussed the challenges associated with maintaining the current level of services provided to the community.

Dr. Wang continued the presentation, speaking to the community paramedicine expansion, the request for staffing in addition of one Community Paramedicine Response Vehicle. C. Braan continued the presentation speaking to the 2024 community paramedicine program.

Chief Crowell responded to questions from the Committee pertaining to funding, investments and the Cambridge Ambulance Communications Centre.

Mathieu Goetzke, Commissioner of Transportation Services, discussed transportation within the Equitable Services and Opportunity strategic priority. He highlighted targeted road safety programs, enhanced partnerships with Townships, context-specific corridor design guidelines, the new Integrated Mobility Plan (Transportation Master Plan), and the expansion of Automated Speed Enforcement. Continuing the presentation, C. Braan provided further details on the 2024 Automated Speed Enforcement Budget.

Committee members engaged in discussions on speeding within Townships, guidelines for community safety zones, funding/financing sources for automated speed enforcement, expansion to school zones, and staffing requirements. Responses to questions were provided by M. Goetzke and C. Dyer.

M. Goetzke continued the presentation, speaking to key 2024 strategic initiatives targeted to improve access to transit, equity in service, planning for future fares, and lowering barriers to transit.

Members of the Committee discussed mobilityPLUS and mitigating transit barriers. Responses to questions were provided by M. Goetzke and C. Dyer.

M. Goetzke continued the presentation, speaking to Provincial fare price and product comparisons, proposed fare changes, and the full overview of proposed GRT fare changes. 

C. Dyer furthered the presentation, providing an update on the 2024 discretionary grants budget, indicating that a report is going to the Administration and Finance Committee with respect to eligibility to the art gallery grant budgets and discretionary grants. 

Addressing Committee inquiries, M. Goetzke provided insights into group passes and transfer windows. He also discussed the possibility of expanding transfer windows, expressing a willingness for staff to explore this option.

notes: Councillor R. Deutschmann indicated his intention to withdraw the motion and noted that he will bring it forward on final budget day.

items.title: Councillor C. James
notes:
Councilor C. James presented an overview of her motion, underscoring its intention to address a notable gap in preparing for the future needs of youth aged 15-24. The focus was on advocating for a strategic budget allocation towards initiatives tailored specifically for this demographic.

Committee members engaged in a discussion on mental health, the impact of domestic violence on youth, the need for youth shelters, housing concerns, and potential funding sources.

The Committee directed staff to report back with a process for the allocation and eligibility of the proposed fund and proposed funding sources.

motions.text: Whereas the Region of Waterloo currently provides the Food Bank of Waterloo Region with an annual funding grant of $744,000.00, And whereas Kim Wilhelm, interim CEO of the Food Bank of Waterloo Region has advised Regional Council that they are seeing the highest numbers in the nearly 40-year history of the foodbank, And whereas more people are facing impossible choices like feeding their children or pay housing costs, or by food or heat their home, And whereas visits to the foodbank totaled 450,387 in 2022/2023, which is almost 2.5 times the number of visits in 2016/2017, And whereas 59,000 people used the food bank program in 2022/2023, up from 30,662 people in 2016/2017 BE IT RESOLVED that the Region of Waterloo increase its annual grant to the Food Bank of Waterloo Region to $1.5 million.
motions.text_html:
Whereas the Region of Waterloo currently provides the Food Bank of Waterloo Region with an annual funding grant of $744,000.00,

And whereas Kim Wilhelm, interim CEO of the Food Bank of Waterloo Region has advised Regional Council that they are seeing the highest numbers in the nearly 40-year history of the foodbank,

And whereas more people are facing impossible choices like feeding their children or pay housing costs, or by food or heat their home,

And whereas visits to the foodbank totaled 450,387 in 2022/2023, which is almost 2.5 times the number of visits in 2016/2017,

And whereas 59,000 people used the food bank program in 2022/2023, up from 30,662 people in 2016/2017

BE IT RESOLVED that the Region of Waterloo increase its annual grant to the Food Bank of Waterloo Region to $1.5 million.

motions.text: Whereas Regional council has established a new 2023-27 strategic plan “Growing with Care” that prioritizes equitable services and opportunities for all, including for children and youth, by providing equitable, accessible, services across Waterloo Region that support the social determinants of health, safety and complete communities as we grow; and WHEREAS the Regional Municipality of Waterloo delivers a variety of programs and services including; Children’s Services; and WHEREAS according to the 2021 Canadian Census, 101, 370 children aged 0 to 14 were counted in the region. Representing approximately 17.3% of the total population. In comparison for Canada the proportion of children was 16.3% in 2023; and WHEREAS youth wellbeing and belonging are increasingly becoming a growing concern in our region; and WHEREAS 1 in 2 youths do not feel like a valued member of our community; and WHEREAS the well-being of youth has been significantly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic; and WHEREAS only 64.1% report a strong sense of belonging to their community, and only 26.3% report positive mental health and these stats are 15, and 54 percentage points lower than pre-pandemic levels, respectively; and WHEREAS there is an increasing need to fill gaps that support youth in the community as their wellbeing and sense of belonging is an integral part of our community, and building upstream community safety; and WHEREAS the region does not currently have a sustainable ongoing program that is specifically targeted to meeting the specific future needs of Youth. Therefore, be it resolved that $500,000 in annual funding be added to the 2024 Regional budget to fund specific priority initiatives that meet the future needs of Youth as has been identified through Community Services, Public Health, the pan-regional collaborative of the adults and young people that come together in the Children and Youth Planning Table, the Smart Waterloo Region Innovation Lab collaborative and The Community Safety and Wellbeing plan.
motions.text_html:
Whereas Regional council has established a new 2023-27 strategic plan “Growing with Care” that prioritizes equitable services and opportunities for all, including for children and youth, by providing equitable, accessible, services across Waterloo Region that support the social determinants of health, safety and complete communities as we grow; and

WHEREAS the Regional Municipality of Waterloo delivers a variety of programs and services including; Children’s Services; and

WHEREAS according to the 2021 Canadian Census, 101, 370 children aged 0 to 14 were counted in the region. Representing approximately 17.3% of the total population. In comparison for Canada the proportion of children was 16.3% in 2023; and

WHEREAS youth wellbeing and belonging are increasingly becoming a growing concern in our region; and

WHEREAS 1 in 2 youths do not feel like a valued member of our community; and

WHEREAS the well-being of youth has been significantly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic; and

WHEREAS only 64.1% report a strong sense of belonging to their community, and only 26.3% report positive mental health and these stats are 15, and 54 percentage points lower than pre-pandemic levels, respectively; and

WHEREAS there is an increasing need to fill gaps that support youth in the community as their wellbeing and sense of belonging is an integral part of our community, and building upstream community safety; and

WHEREAS the region does not currently have a sustainable ongoing program that is specifically targeted to meeting the specific future needs of Youth. 

Therefore, be it resolved that $500,000 in annual funding be added to the 2024 Regional budget to fund specific priority initiatives that meet the future needs of Youth as has been identified through Community Services, Public Health, the pan-regional collaborative of the adults and young people that come together in the Children and Youth Planning Table, the Smart Waterloo Region Innovation Lab collaborative and The Community Safety and Wellbeing plan.
